cost: TWO PINS WERE RELEASED BY HIM AND RE-PINNED HERE, both moved to data/anchors_superseded.json with his words. Stephen Curry '16 off 95 +-1 (recal_89) -> 99 +-1, note "Tomer 2026-09-30: 'Curry 16 OFF too low'". LeBron James '13 off 97 +-1 (recal_89) -> 99 +-1, note "Tomer 2026-09-30: 'Push 227 with LeBron 13 released if needed'". LeBron '13 is NOT collateral the round chose: his signature is 95.06, the second-highest of 10,000, so any term that pays the top of that distribution pays him at least as much as the subject. The amendment is what makes the round landable at 99 rather than 98.

THE COST IS THE SUMMIT'S TIE BLOCK, and it is recal_102's own trade taken one step further. Cards printing OFF 99 go from 15 to 26. recal_102 put seventeen there on his instruction ("Jordan still too low. I want him 98+ OFF and DEF") by setting OFF_TOP 102.75 BELOW the measured maximum, so everything above the constant clamps; this round adds eleven cards that were already at 95-98 and are now past it. The band was NOT re-derived and no card above the knee is re-mapped — but the raw the band clamps moved a long way: the pool's raw OFF top is now Michael Jordan '89 at 111.3213 (was Giannis Antetokounmpo '25 at 108.0222) and 24 cards sit above OFF_TOP where 21 did. A future round that re-derives OFF_TOP will therefore find a much higher number than recal_90 measured, and the doctrine recal_102 overturned ("the top is the MEASURED MAXIMUM RAW") is now three points further from the constant.

THE DOMINANCE BONUS IS STILL THE OPEN CONFLICT recal_210 REPORTED, and this round deliberately does not touch it. recal_210 measured that the only monotone form of the towering test (read the weapon against a FIXED bar, drop `z[0] > z[1] + z[2]` and the 1.5 clause) breaks Malik Beasley '23 58 +-3 -> 53 and Donyell Marshall '07 52 +-3 -> 48 as well as lifting Curry '16 and LeBron '13, and 877 cards move. Two of those four pins are now released, but the two SHOOTER pins are not, and the form still cannot reach 99 on the subject in any case (+2.27 of o_score at most, gate_f pinned on its 0.25 floor). So recal_210's law — 478 cards / 867 (card,bar) pairs on the whole o_score, zone block 0 — is unchanged by this round, which reads no zone bar at all.

THE CLASS THIS TERM PRICES IS SMALL AND IT IS NOW MOSTLY AT THE CEILING. Nine cards of 10,000 saturate the gate (signature > 91.20) and eleven more are on the ramp. Eight of the sixteen movers land on 99, so a later ruling that wants to separate Adrian Dantley '80-'82, Karl Malone '90, LeBron '14 or Shaquille O'Neal '02/'03 from the subject cannot do it inside o_score without moving OFF_TOP or the 0.93 multiplier. Adrian Dantley '81 (97 -> 99) is the largest unpinned rise and the one to watch: 30.7 points on .626 true shooting, volume 94 / efficiency 99, OVR 82 -> 83 because his defence carries the card down.
notes: HIS RULING, verbatim: "Curry 16' OFF too low." And the amendment that arrived mid-round, verbatim: "Push 227 with LeBron '13 released if needed." The target read off his words is 99 — the unanimous MVP, 30.1 ppg on .669 TS at 32.6% usage, with Michael Jordan '89, Kevin Durant '14 and Nikola Jokić '25.

THE CARD, DECOMPOSED FIRST, AND THE POINT IS THAT NOTHING IS MISSING FROM IT. o_score 104.0142 = z[0] 21.780 + z[1] 6.480 + z[2] 3.700 + efficiency 10.780 + volume x load 23.801 + playvol x load 16.340 + ballsec 6.700 + fouldraw x ft 5.005 + orb 1.980 + signature 7.448. Raw 96.7332, printed 95. No bonus fires: recal_37/38's zone-dominance gate demands the weapon tower over the OTHER TWO ZONES PUT TOGETHER and 99 < 81 + 74, so the greatest three-point season the file holds is read as having no weapon. recal_198's third level does not fire either: his third zone is 74.0, exactly the ramp's foot. No floor touches him.

WHY THE BONUS IS NOT THE ANSWER, MEASURED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS WRITTEN. recal_210 already measured the only monotone repair of the towering test and recorded that it reads this card 97, not 99 — and the arithmetic says why: a SHOOTER's bonus is gated on the offence he already has (recal_44, gate_f = 1.00 - (pre_off - 55) x 0.025), and at pre_off 96.73 the subject sits on that gate's FLOOR of 0.25. His whole reachable bonus is 5.0 x 1.10 x 1.65 x 0.25 = +2.27 of o_score. The ruling needs +5.60 (raw 101.9375 is the band's own 98.5 line, o_score 109.61). The dominance bonus is provably short by more than a factor of two, whatever is done to its shape.

SO THE TERM THAT IS SHORT IS THE ONE THE RULING NAMES. recal_26's SIGNATURE, 0.08 x volume x efficiency / 100, is LINEAR IN THE PRODUCT across the whole board: the step from a median pair to a good one and the step from a top-1% pair to the best one ever are paid at the same 0.08 a point. The subject's product is 93.10 against the pool's median 27.72, p99 80.36 and maximum 96.03 — fourth of 10,000 — and the whole of his lead over James Harden '19 (86.13) is worth 0.56 of o_score. A signature that cannot separate the top of its own distribution is not pricing a signature.

THE FIX IS recal_198's, APPLIED TO recal_198's OWN GATE. That round paid the THIRD ZONE a second time at its own standing weight once the signature cleared the pool's top percentiles, and stated in terms that "the product is the GATE, it cannot be the payload" — because the ruling it was landing (Kevin Durant '13 over LeBron James '13) was ordered the WRONG way by the product, five to one. THIS ruling is ordered the RIGHT way by it: Curry '16 93.10 against Harden '19 86.13 and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander '25 86.24, and his amendment has released the one card the product puts above the subject. So the payload can be the product here, and it is the product's own standing weight paid a second time. No new weight is introduced, exactly as recal_198 introduced none.

EVERY CONSTANT IS A PERCENTILE OF THE POOL, MEASURED, NOT CHOSEN. SIG2_HI = 91.20 is the pool's p99.9 of volume x efficiency / 100 — the dispatch's own phrase, 'a top-0.1% pair', turned into a number; 9 cards of 10,000 clear it. SIG2_LO = 89.182 is p99.8, so the gate FADES IN over the last tenth of a percentile instead of stepping at it (recal_93/99/136/137/154/164's rule that every gate in this file is a ramp); 20 cards clear the foot. SIG2_K = 0.08 is the signature's own weight, and recal_130's doctrine follows it — 'a rate paid twice is scaled twice' — so the second payment is scaled by recal_163's SECOND_FULL = 33.9. The subject plays 34.2 and is paid in full: 0.08 x 93.10 x 1.0000 x 1.0000 = +7.448.

THE FOOT IS NOT FREE AND THE ROUND SAYS WHICH CARD SETS IT. At the pool's p99.5 (85.36) the term pays Karl Malone '99 +5.7 and takes him 91 -> 93 — which is recal_98's ruling, in his own words 'How is Karl Malone 99 is 93 OFF? ... Eff is good but nothing crazy..', undone exactly. His signature is 87.30. At p99.7 (87.30) he sits precisely ON the foot and the gate is closed on him, which is a knife-edge; at p99.8 (89.182) he is 1.88 clear of it. p99.8 is also the narrowest of the reaching feet by collateral — 16 movers against 22 at p99.7 and 32 at p99.5 — which is recal_137's rule for choosing a width ('the round takes the narrowest width that reaches both numbers').

PROVABLY DISJOINT FROM EVERY FLOOR AND FROM THE CHARGE, by recal_198's own argument one rung higher. The gate needs volume >= 90.1 (efficiency is capped at 99), while recal_64's off-ball floor, recal_91's stretch-big floor, recal_155's two-level term, recal_182's glue floor and recal_186's glass floor all gate on volume < 55; recal_109's elite-passer band tops out at volume 93 with an efficiency gate; and the turnover charge needs efficiency < 60, so sig <= 59.4. The term is LAST in o_score, after recal_198's, so no floor's `_fl > std` comparison sees it.

MEASURED on all 10,000 cards: 16 move on OFF, EVERY ONE OF THEM UP, max +4; 15 follow on OVR; DEF, every attribute, the big flag and is_big move on ZERO. The movers are one class and read like it — the whole top of the volume x efficiency distribution and nothing else: Stephen Curry '15/'16, Kevin Durant '12/'13/'16, LeBron James '13/'14, Adrian Dantley '80/'81/'82, Karl Malone '90/'92/'98, Shaquille O'Neal '02/'03, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander '26. Every one of the 220 anchors passes except the two he released.

recal_210's MONOTONICITY LAW IS UNTOUCHED BY CONSTRUCTION: this term reads no zone bar, so d(std)/d(rim) = d(std)/d(mid) = d(std)/d(3pt) = 0 on its line. The zone block stays at 0 inverting cards and the whole-o_score count, the conflict recal_210 reported open, falls 580 -> 478 cards (1003 -> 867 pairs) because more of the dominance bonus's inverting cards are now clamped at the ceiling.
